question: How do paragraph 14 and footnote 5 attach the request trigger, object and standard of confirmation and demonstration? What follows when no SFC request has been made, and how do paragraphs 15 and 16 differ? Preserve supported rival readings.

26EC22:10.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

26EC22:11.quote: Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

26EC22:12.quote: Product Providers should have appropriate measures in place to manage and mitigate cybersecurity risks3, data privacy, system outages and recovery, and maintain a comprehensive and robust business continuity plan.

26EC22:13.quote: Product Providers should not use public-permissionless blockchain networks without additional and proper controls (eg, Product Providers to impose additional control by using a permissioned token)4.

26EC22:14.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

26EC22:15.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.

26EC22:16.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain satisfactory legal opinion to support its application.

26EC22:FN1.quote: 1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

26EC22:FN5.quote: 5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Appendix:audit.quote: If the intermediary relies on a smart contract audit conducted by a third party, it should be able to demonstrate that it is reasonable to rely on such smart contract audit. The smart contract audit should focus on reviewing whether the smart contract is not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

reasoning.text: On the main-text reading, confirmation is standing while demonstration is conditional on an SFC request. The stated object includes management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity; the demonstration is to the SFC’s satisfaction. Absence of a request answers activation of this demonstration limb only.

Footnote 5 says “confirm and demonstrate” without repeating the request qualification. A standing-demonstration reading therefore remains a rival. Reading the footnote as specifying the content of the main paragraph preserves the request qualification; treating it as an additional standing obligation does not. No inspected express priority rule conclusively resolves that attachment.

The Appendix places “with a high level of confidence” specifically in the technical smart-contract audit discussion. That supports technical attachment of the similar footnote language, without proving it exclusively qualifies that limb. Wider evidential attachment remains possible. The Appendix is non-exhaustive and referred to where applicable; it supplies no numerical threshold and does not equate technical confidence with SFC satisfaction.

Paragraph 15 separately concerns obtaining third-party audit or verification, on request, of the stated operational, record and contract matters. Paragraph 16 concerns obtaining a satisfactory legal opinion, on request, to support the application. Neither procurement is identical to the paragraph-14 demonstration, and neither substitutes automatically for confirmation or the underlying paragraphs 10–13 requirements.

A report on contract V1 does not establish assurance about a materially changed deployed V2. Reliance needs a basis connecting scope, method and version to the arrangement. Even an adequate technical report does not itself establish that the SFC is satisfied.

conditions.then: Main-text demonstration is not shown activated; confirmation and underlying duties remain, and the footnote rival remains open.

conditions.if: A request is established but demonstration is inadequate
conditions.then: The requested-demonstration condition is not fulfilled on that reading.
Only that scoped condition is fulfilled; confirmation, paragraphs 10–13 and separate requests need their own assessment.
Keep both branches conditional; unknown is not no request.

facts_required: Whether, when and for what scope the SFC requested demonstration, audit/verification or legal opinion.
What was confirmed and by whom; deployed contract and audit versions; identified flaws and changes.
Basis for reliance on third-party work and the actual SFC response.
remaining_limits: Attachment and legal priority remain unresolved.
No client compliance or numerical confidence conclusion.
